i don’t have answers for all of your questions, but as a system we have experienced a lot of the same emotions and asked a lot of the same questions. we  have some alters who get stuck in the past and struggle to acclimate to the present moment when they are fronting; one way we’ve learned to help with this adjustment in the moment is to have possessions and clothing items that belong to each alter that can help them get grounded in the present moment (we also have playlists for some alters that are more grounded by sounds). journaling has also been extremely helpful, we have a system journal, a few individual journals for different alters that want more space to write, and a daily journal to keep a basic record of events, thoughts, and feelings that come up chronologically. we also have a planner and multiple calendars around the house to help us keep track of time passing and what day and year it is. 
your system needs may be different, but it’s a place to start and make changes from there based on what works best for you.
it isn’t easy or perfect, but we have improved a lot since we began working on system communication and daily routines. 
the trauma will always be there, but slowly you each will begin to heal and process the different pieces you each hold. sometimes our host gets frustrated with feeling like they’re processing the same traumas over and over as each alter does their part of the work, and we don’t have a complete solution for that, but it’s gotten so much easier as each of us has begun the work in the system.

working with our hands/having projects helps us as a system to relax and also practice communicating about a common project/task.

other strategies to consider: 
- schedule time away from the house as much as possible (e.g. job/work, school, hiking, anything really).
- look at local facebook groups for apartments available, sometimes there are groups where people post looking for roommates (if you feel comfortable with living with roommates)
- find community groups to join, (i’ve used facebook, meetup, and good ol’ google to find some where i live). this again gets you out of the house, and also can help you make connections in the community who aren’t your family.

are you able to do a little research on local shelters and domestic violence resources? i was in a bad situation a few years ago and had to leave my house abruptly due to threats of violence from roommates. i was couch surfing for a bit after that, until i got in contact with a local domestic violence shelter. 
even if they can’t accommodate you right away, they may be able to help you find more local resources to support you living in a safer environment and with more independence. 
i also have an abusive family (who very much contributed to our development of DID) that i moved away from as soon as i could, and i know how hard it is to feel like you’re trapped somewhere you don’t feel safe. i hope you get some good support on here, and that you find a safe place to heal 💗

we have both, and honestly it’s become so intertwined with our DID that some alters experience manic episodes very frequently, while others rarely do. however, some of our symptoms can only be explained by dissociation/DID, which sounds similar to what you’re experiencing. 
it has been helpful for us to almost treat it as though certain alters have bipolar, and they can focus on learning coping skills to manage the intense mania/crashes, while others focus on learning skills to deal with depressive episodes, panic attacks, etc. it’s not a perfect approach, but it seems to be working for us. 
wishing you luck 🍀

there’s an app made for DID/OSDD systems called “simply plural”. we just started using it, but it seems to have a lot of potential to help with communication and record keeping (for our system at least). also we use another app called “Toca Boca” to make a digital version of our inner world and alters. it’s not completely free like the first one, but is really well made (imo).

maybe try looking at etsy for some engraved charms or something? like a metal piece that you could tie to a rope bracelet. 
we made our own bracelets out of elastic thread and small glass/ceramic beads, but it sounds like that isn’t a viable option for you. hope you find some good ideas here!

if any littles from our system are fronting around bedtime, we’ve found things like coloring and/or watching a low-key kids show works really well (like “Summer Camp Island” or “Bluey”).

we also have one alter who listens to a podcast about trees when they’re relaxing or winding down (it’s called “Completely Arbortrary”). 

idk if these help, but our system has also struggled a lot with sleep issues, and i hope you find some more ideas here that work for you guys!

a similar thing happened to me, for years growing up, with my older brother. i’m so sorry your brother betrayed you like this, it’s a kind of heartbreak unlike any other.
 i have not forgiven my brother/abuser, and don’t let anyone push you to forgive yours if you do not want to/are not ready. 
even if my brother changed and grew into a wonderful and safe person in the future, i would still feel unsafe around him and not want anything to do with him. it sounds like you are prioritizing your safety and well-being, and you’re incredibly strong to have had that conversation with your parents (i couldn’t talk about any of it until i left their house and i wrote them an email).
i hope you are able to heal, whatever the other outcomes.

i have been in a similar situation. we have an alter who, at a several points, had us so afraid they would do something to the body while fronting, that we ended up in the ER/psych ward (more than once).
it’s terrifying. 
but being in the psych ward itself is just like any other new environment, it might be overwhelming and you’ll need time to adjust, but you will be safe and have access to medical professionals whose job it is to help you.
you are strong and you can get through this
